_comment: The hierarchy the deploy script converges the chain to. Declarative and idempotent: run it
again and it registers only what is missing.
FOUR LEVELS: canopy.eth (platform) -> issuer -> broker -> investor.
ISSUERS are the platform's counterparties. Each gets a UserRegistry, a name under canopy.eth,
setParent wired back, and its OWN ENSAllowlistChecker bound to its own pool token. Give them a
long ttl: an issuer lapsing cascades to every broker and investor beneath it, which is a much
bigger event than the one we film.
BROKERS are the issuer's distribution. A broker onboarded by two issuers appears TWICE, with
the same label under different issuers — that is the intended way to express it. The proxy salt
and the address-book key both include the issuer, so the two never collide.
INVESTORS listed here are BOOTSTRAP ONLY. In the real flow they arrive via an application ->
CRE verdict -> MintAttestor (beats 1-4). Keep this list to the few needed before CRE exists,
and to the ones the demo needs guaranteed present. Adding everyone here bypasses the product.
wallet: leave empty to derive a deterministic placeholder. Placeholders CANNOT SIGN, so any
investor who has to transact on camera needs a real address here. Wallets must be distinct
WITHIN an issuer — one checker holds one leaf per account — but the same wallet may legitimately
hold a name under both issuers.
ttl: seconds until the name expires. 0 means take the BROKER_TTL env default, which the demo
shortens to film the lapse. Only the broker being filmed should get the short value; give every
other broker an explicit long ttl, or a global short TTL expires all of them at once and the
cascade looks like a kill switch rather than something scoped to one issuer's one broker.
